clue.text: Lower colour on wrong cue

indicators.note: letters set down wrongly are out of their proper order and must be rearranged

blocks.note: red is a colour
the letters of cue, rearranged

explanation.surface: A snooker player paints the cue the wrong colour and must tone it down.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower something is to bring down its level or amount, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Going up to teacher to get food

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters run from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
pupils address a male teacher as sir
the second to, taken as written

explanation.surface: A pupil goes up to the teacher's desk to collect their lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first two words after the indicator turn round; the final to is added unchanged afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish, so it is an example of food.

clue.text: Small scotch, perhaps, before a show?

blocks.note: a dram is a small measure of whisky, such as scotch
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has a quick whisky before going to the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play, the kind of performance staged as a theatre show.

clue.text: Weapon for slight girl

blocks.note: to cut someone is to slight or snub them
lass is a northern British and Scottish word for a girl

explanation.surface: Choosing a suitable weapon for a girl of slender build.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword once carried by sailors and pirates.

clue.text: Fail by two points miserably in the end

indicators.note: done miserably means done badly, leaving the letters in a poor jumbled state

blocks.note: taken as written
north and east are two compass points

explanation.surface: A student fails an exam by just two marks and ends up miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: A finale is the closing part of a show or piece of music, its concluding section.

clue.text: Smooth one, first clever then sarcastic

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: to iron is to smooth out creases
the Roman numeral for one
the opening letter of clever

explanation.surface: A smooth talker starts out clever and turns sarcastic.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironic remarks say the opposite of what is meant, close in sense to mocking or sarcastic.

clue.text: US collection for Marie, upset at scene of wedding

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
Cana in Galilee is where the Bible sets the wedding feast at which water became wine

explanation.surface: Marie is distressed at a wedding, perhaps an American one.
explanation.definitionFit: Americana are artefacts and memorabilia relating to the United States, gathered as a collection.

clue.text: Butler gets nowhere, sadly, in his imaginary state

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A butler fails to advance, sadly, while in an agitated state.
explanation.walkthrough: Butler here is Samuel Butler, the Victorian novelist, not a servant; his satirical utopia is named with nowhere almost spelt backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Erewhon is the fictional country in Samuel Butler's 1872 satirical novel, so his invented land.

clue.text: For instance, De Freitas to try jumper on the Queen

blocks.note: to try something is to test it
a cricket is a jumping insect
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: Someone named De Freitas tries a sweater on the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumper is British for a sweater, which is the false path; here it is the hopping insect. Phillip DeFreitas played cricket for England in the 1980s and 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: DeFreitas played Test matches for England, making him an example of an international cricketer.

clue.text: Some wet themselves, whereas I am continent

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is wanted

blocks.note: the letters run across where, as, I and am

explanation.surface: A smug remark: some people wet themselves, but I can hold it.
explanation.walkthrough: Continent is read in its sense of self-controlled bladder, the opposite of incontinent, until it turns out to be a landmass.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest of the world's continents, an example of the category.

clue.text: See Honest Joe initially organised to keep up with this family

definitions.text: to keep up with this family
definitions.note: the definition leans on the idiom keeping up with the Joneses

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the name before it
organised means put into a fresh arrangement, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of Joe

explanation.surface: Honest Joe arranges things so the family can match the neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: To keep up with the Joneses is to compete with neighbours in visible wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: In the idiom about matching neighbours' possessions, the Joneses are the archetypal family one tries to rival.

clue.text: Love to race away, mostly to the city

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like O
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A romantic dash away to the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is a city, the capital of Canada, in Ontario.

clue.text: Perverted wit amusing at dusk

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of its proper form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
light entertainment is amusing rather than serious

explanation.surface: Smutty humour goes down well in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight is the dim period after sunset, the same time of day as dusk.

clue.text: History loses nothing following bribe? The argument's persuasive but wrong!

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the noun

indicators.note: a word that loses something has a letter taken out of it

blocks.note: a sop is a small concession offered to placate someone
taken as written
nothing is zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A cynic says history is rewritten by bribery and its arguments are slick but false.
explanation.walkthrough: Following puts the bribe in front of the shortened history.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophistry is the use of clever-sounding but fallacious reasoning to deceive or persuade.

clue.text: Courage overcoming pain and sorrow

blocks.note: to have heart is to have courage
an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: Bravery triumphs over suffering and grief.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, overcoming means sitting on top of, so the courage sits above the pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is emotional anguish or grief, matching sorrow as a near synonym.

clue.text: Sound head of hair for the most part

definitions.note: from the phrase in the main, meaning mostly

indicators.note: sound means we go by how the phrase is spoken, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: a mane is a long thick head of hair

explanation.surface: Someone's hair is mostly healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: The main part is the chief or greater part, as in the idiom in the main, meaning mostly.

clue.text: Cheek of the fellow!

blocks.note: first meaning: the jaw or cheek, as in chops
second meaning: a man, an informal word for a bloke

explanation.surface: An indignant exclamation at someone's impudence.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheek reads as impudence, but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap is an old word for the jaw or cheek, and also everyday British slang for a man.

clue.text: In church, one bishop on his feet and all of a twitter!

definitions.note: a phrase for the verb, twitter meaning birdsong

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
the Roman numeral for one
RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title
standing up means on one's feet

explanation.surface: A bishop rises in church, agitated and excited.
explanation.walkthrough: All of a twitter suggests nervous excitement, but twitter is birdsong here.
explanation.definitionFit: To chirrup is to make the short high chirping sounds of a small bird, as twittering does.

clue.text: A high point after turn No. 4 gets things moving

definitions.note: a verb phrase for the noun

indicators.note: after sends the A and the high point behind the turn and its number, reversing the clue's order

blocks.note: a turn is a performer's act
IV is four in Roman numerals
taken as written
a tor is a rocky hilltop on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A climactic moment after the fourth act livens up the show.
explanation.walkthrough: After puts the A and the hilltop behind the turn and its number.
explanation.definitionFit: An activator is something that starts a process or sets it working.

clue.text: Driven at home, having vision, they say

indicators.note: they say points to what people speak aloud rather than what is written

blocks.note: being in means being at home
sighted means able to see

explanation.surface: Someone driven home said to have had a vision.
explanation.definitionFit: To be incited is to be urged or spurred on to act, as one is driven to do something.

clue.text: Remain until the very end

blocks.note: surface reading: stay to the close of an event
setter's reading: still be there after everyone else has gone

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is simply a description; staying longer than the others is the sense wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlast someone is to survive or endure longer than they do.

clue.text: Take exception to an item

blocks.note: first meaning: protest against, as a verb
second meaning: a thing, as a noun

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a particular thing.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to protest or disapprove, and as a noun it means a physical thing.

clue.text: This measure can be a mere bagatelle!

blocks.note: a pint is a measure of liquid
if you can, you are able

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark that a single drink is a trifle.
explanation.walkthrough: A mere bagatelle means a trifle; bagatelle is also a pub game played on a pin table.
explanation.definitionFit: A pintable is a board game like pinball, and bagatelle is a game played on one.

clue.text: Pursued, reportedly, by the virtuous

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard spoken, so the sound counts rather than spelling

blocks.note: pursued means chased

explanation.surface: Someone is said to be pursued by righteous people.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means sexually pure or morally upright, so close in sense to virtuous.

clue.text: Perish, dressed in gold - farewell!

indicators.note: dressed in means clothed, wrapped by something outside it

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to perish is to die

explanation.surface: A dramatic goodbye: die wearing gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a French-derived word of parting, used in English to mean goodbye.

clue.text: Trace incident in sporting competition

blocks.note: to trace something is to track it
an incident is an event

explanation.surface: Following up an incident that happened at a sports meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A track event is a running race in athletics, one of the competitions at a meeting.

clue.text: I married a third woman, being a caliph

indicators.note: third asks for the letter in third position of the following word

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for married
taken as written
the third letter of woman

explanation.surface: A man confesses to taking a third wife, as a caliph might.
explanation.definitionFit: Imam was a title of the caliphs as leaders of the Muslim community.

clue.text: Sufficient to supply half around hospital department

indicators.note: half means only part of the word is kept and the rest is dropped
around means the shortened word wraps itself about the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: Enough provisions to stock half a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the second half of supply survives, then it opens up to take the department inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty means a sufficient or ample quantity, as in there is plenty.

clue.text: Adapt to the present time - barely!

blocks.note: AD, anno Domini, labels the current era
just means barely, as in only just

explanation.surface: Someone only barely manages to fit in with modern times.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust is to alter or modify something to suit conditions, a synonym of adapt.
